b.x: Advent begins in the garden, right after the first sin. Before God sends Adam and Eve out, he tells the serpent that a descendant of the woman will one day crush its head ([Genesis 3:15](Gen.3.15)). Christian readers have long called this verse the first announcement of the gospel.

c.x: War is proclaimed between the Seed of the woman and the seed of the serpent.
[Read the full comment](commentary:matthewHenry/Gen.3.14-Gen.3.15)
her offspring (literally her seed): This collective noun can refer to a single descendant or many.
[Read the study note](commentary:tyndale/Gen.3.15)

b.x: God calls Abram away from his home and promises that through him all the families of the earth will be blessed. Paul reads this promise as the gospel announced in advance, fulfilled for everyone who shares Abraham's faith ([Galatians 3:8](Gal.3.8)).

c.x: This certainly is an inestimable pledge of special love, that God should so greatly condescend for our sake.
[Read the full comment](commentary:calvin/Gen.12.3)

b.x: David wants to build God a house, but God promises to build David a house instead: a dynasty and a throne that will last forever ([2 Samuel 7:16](2Sam.7.16)). Later prophets and the Gospel writers return to this promise again and again.

c.x: The establishing of his house, his throne, and his kingdom for ever, can be applied to no other than to Christ and his kingdom: David's house and kingdom long since came to an end.
[Read the full comment](commentary:matthewHenry/2Sam.7.4-2Sam.7.17)

b.x: [David](people:David) · [God's Covenant with David](themes:GodsCovenantWithDavid) · [The Promise of Dynasty](themes:ThePromiseOfDynasty)
When King Ahaz refuses to ask for a sign, God gives one anyway: a child named Immanuel, "God with us." Matthew later quotes this verse in his account of Jesus' birth ([Matthew 1:23](Matt.1.23)).

c.x: This prophecy received its ultimate fulfillment in the birth of Jesus Christ (Matt 1:18-24). Yet it is likely that it also had a partial fulfillment in Isaiah's day.
[Read the study note](commentary:tyndale/Isa.7.14)

b.x: "The people walking in darkness have seen a great light." Isaiah promises a child who will carry the government on his shoulders and whose kingdom of peace will never end.

c.x: In the Messiah's kingdom, the darkness would give way to great light, which was to dawn in Galilee and reach the whole nation, and then the whole world.
[Read the study note](commentary:tyndale/Isa.9.1-Isa.9.7)

b.x: David's family tree looks cut down, but Isaiah sees a new shoot growing from the stump of Jesse. The Spirit of the Lord will rest on him, and he will rule with justice for the poor.

c.x: This new growth refers to the continuity of David's royal family line despite its virtual cessation during the Exile.
[Read the study note](commentary:tyndale/Isa.11.1)

b.x: Micah names a small town, Bethlehem, as the birthplace of a ruler "whose origins are from of old." The chief priests point Herod to this verse when the wise men arrive ([Matthew 2:5–6](Matt.2.5-Matt.2.6)).

c.x: In the future, an even more significant ruler than David would arise from there.
[Read the study note](commentary:tyndale/Mic.5.2)

b.x: The second week turns to preparation. Isaiah opens his message of comfort with a voice calling out to prepare the way of the Lord in the wilderness, the same words the Gospels use for John the Baptist ([Mark 1:3](Mark.1.3)).

c.x: He therefore testifies that "the wilderness" shall not hinder them from enjoying that consolation.
[Read the full comment](commentary:calvin/Isa.40.3)

b.x: Malachi's name means "my messenger," and he promises one who will prepare the way before the Lord comes to his temple. Jesus later points to this verse when he speaks about John ([Matthew 11:10](Matt.11.10)).

c.x: Jesus identified John the Baptist by pointing to this passage (see Matt 11:10; Mark 1:2; Luke 7:27).
[Read the study note](commentary:tyndale/Mal.3.1)

b.x: The Old Testament closes with a promise that the sun of righteousness will rise with healing in its wings, and that God will send Elijah before the great day of the Lord.

c.x: In both, Christ is a rejoicing Light to those who serve him faithfully. By the Sun of Righteousness we understand Jesus Christ.
[Read the full comment](commentary:matthewHenry/Mal.4.1-Mal.4.3)

b.x: After centuries of silence, the angel Gabriel appears to an elderly priest. His son John will go before the Lord "in the spirit and power of Elijah" ([Luke 1:17](Luke.1.17)), the very promise Malachi ended with.

c.x: The calling of John had no other design than to secure for Christ a willing ear.
[Read the full comment](commentary:calvin/Luke.1.17)

b.x: Mark starts his Gospel with Isaiah and Malachi, then introduces John baptizing in the wilderness. John's message points away from himself to one who is mightier.

c.x: This account is not primarily about John the Baptist, the messenger, but about the one he announces.
[Read the study note](commentary:tyndale/Mark.1.2-Mark.1.8)

b.x: John calls Israel to repent because the kingdom of heaven is near. He warns the religious leaders that ancestry is no substitute for fruit, and he says he is not worthy even to carry the sandals of the one coming after him.

c.x: Despite his popularity and growing following, John had a clear sense of his role as subordinate to the Messiah.
[Read the study note](commentary:tyndale/Matt.3.11)

b.x: John's Gospel describes the Baptist as a witness who came to testify about the light. When the leaders ask who he is, he answers only with Isaiah's words: a voice in the wilderness.

c.x: John disowns himself to be the Christ, who was now expected and waited for.
[Read the full comment](commentary:matthewHenry/John.1.19-John.1.28)

b.x: The third week turns to the announcement. Gabriel tells Mary she will bear a son who will receive the throne of his father David, the promise from week one. Mary answers, "I am the Lord's servant."

c.x: The angel does not explain the manner, so as to satisfy curiosity, which there was no necessity for doing.
[Read the full comment](commentary:calvin/Luke.1.35)

b.x: [Mary, Mother of Jesus](people:Mary-MotherofJesus) · [Gabriel](dictionary:Gabriel) · [The Son of God](themes:TheSonOfGod)
Matthew tells the story from Joseph's side. An angel tells him to name the child Jesus, "because he will save his people from their sins," and Matthew connects the birth to Isaiah's sign of Immanuel.

c.x: The angel expresses the reason why the Son of God is so called, Because he shall SAVE his people.
[Read the full comment](commentary:calvin/Matt.1.21)

b.x: When Mary arrives, the unborn John leaps in Elizabeth's womb, and Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Spirit, calls Mary "the mother of my Lord."

c.x: It is very good for those who have the work of grace begun in their souls, to communicate one to another.
[Read the full comment](commentary:matthewHenry/Luke.1.39-Luke.1.56)

b.x: Mary praises God her Savior, who lifts up the humble and fills the hungry with good things. Her song echoes Hannah's prayer ([1 Samuel 2:1–10](1Sam.2.1-1Sam.2.10)) and ends with God's promise to Abraham.

c.x: The fact that God cares for the oppressed and reverses their fortunes is a common theme throughout Luke's Gospel.
[Read the study note](commentary:tyndale/Luke.1.46-Luke.1.55)

b.x: At John's naming, Zechariah writes "His name is John" and his voice returns. The neighbors are left asking what this child will become.

c.x: Unbelief closed his mouth, and believing opened it again.
[Read the full comment](commentary:matthewHenry/Luke.1.57-Luke.1.66)

b.x: Zechariah's song praises God for remembering his covenant and describes the coming salvation as a sunrise: "the dawn from on high" that gives light to those who sit in darkness.

c.x: The Messiah is identified in the Old Testament as a light shining in darkness (Isa 9:2; 42:6-7; 49:6; Mal 4:2).
[Read the study note](commentary:tyndale/Luke.1.78)

b.x: Isaiah pictures a messenger running over the hills to a ruined Jerusalem with the news that God reigns. Paul applies these words to everyone who brings the gospel ([Romans 10:15](Rom.10.15)).

c.x: The imagery is of a besieged city waiting for word that its hero has defeated the enemy armies.
[Read the study note](commentary:tyndale/Isa.52.7-Isa.52.12)

b.x: The final week turns to the arrival. Matthew opens with a genealogy that runs from Abraham through David to Jesus, tying together the promises from the first week.

c.x: The promise of the blessing was made to Abraham and his seed; of the dominion, to David and his seed.
[Read the full comment](commentary:matthewHenry/Matt.1.1-Matt.1.17)

t: In the Beginning Was the Word

b.x: John begins his Gospel before Bethlehem, in the beginning with God. Everything was made through the Word, and the light shines in the darkness.

c.x: The darkness would try to destroy Jesus (the light), but it would fail.
[Read the study note](commentary:tyndale/John.1.5)

b.x: The true light comes into the world, and the Word becomes flesh and lives among us. John says that those who receive him are given the right to become children of God.

c.x: Although the Evangelist touches briefly the unutterable mystery, that the Son of God was clothed with human nature, yet this brevity is wonderfully perspicuous.
[Read the full comment](commentary:calvin/John.1.14)

b.x: Paul describes Christ taking the form of a servant and being born in human likeness. He uses this to call the Philippians to the same humility.

c.x: he gave up his divine privileges (literally he emptied himself): The rest of 2:7-8 explains this ultimate expression of divine self-denial.
[Read the study note](commentary:tyndale/Phil.2.7)

t: When the Time Had Fully Come

b.x: On Christmas Eve, Paul's summary and Luke's story meet. God sent his Son, born of a woman, at the right time, and Mary lays her firstborn in a manger because there is no room for them.

c.x: Although he was the glorious Messiah, Jesus entered the world in humble circumstances.
[Read the study note](commentary:tyndale/Luke.2.1-Luke.2.7)

b.x: On Christmas Day, angels announce the birth to shepherds: "Unto you is born this day in the city of David a Savior, who is Christ the Lord." The shepherds go, see, and spread the news.

c.x: This day is born the Redeemer long ago promised, who was to restore the Church of God to its proper condition.
[Read the full comment](commentary:calvin/Luke.2.11)
